contents.en: The universe expands from an extremely hot, dense state, setting the stage for matter, galaxies, and eventually the atoms that make up every modern technology.
contents.ru: Вселенная расширяется из крайне горячего и плотного состояния, создавая условия для вещества, галактик и, в конечном счёте, атомов, из которых состоит любая современная технология.
contents.it: L'universo si espande da uno stato estremamente caldo e denso, preparando la scena per la materia, le galassie e, infine, gli atomi che compongono ogni tecnologia moderna.
contents.de: Das Universum dehnt sich aus einem extrem heißen, dichten Zustand aus und bereitet die Bühne für Materie, Galaxien und schließlich die Atome, aus denen jede moderne Technik besteht.
contents.es: El universo se expande desde un estado extremadamente caliente y denso, preparando el escenario para la materia, las galaxias y, finalmente, los átomos que forman toda la tecnología moderna.

contents.en: Within a few hundred million years of the Big Bang, gravity gathers primordial hydrogen and helium into dense clouds. Traces of molecular hydrogen let the gas radiate heat and cool, so it can collapse further and give birth to the first stars.
The first stars forge heavy elements in their cores and disperse them when they die, providing the raw materials for planets and life.
Accretion of dust and rock builds planet Earth. Its crust, oceans, and atmosphere begin to form over the next hundreds of millions of years.

A Mars-sized body, Theia, strikes the young Earth. The debris thrown into orbit gathers into the Moon within a few million years.

The Moon stabilizes the tilt of Earth's axis, which keeps the climate steady over long spans, and raises tides that later shape shorelines and coastal life.
contents.ru:
Тело размером с Марс, Тейя, сталкивается с молодой Землёй. Выброшенные на орбиту обломки за несколько миллионов лет собираются в Луну.

Луна стабилизирует наклон земной оси, благодаря чему климат остаётся устойчивым в течение долгих эпох, и вызывает приливы, которые позже формируют береговые линии и прибрежную жизнь.
contents.it:
Un corpo grande come Marte, Theia, colpisce la giovane Terra. I detriti scagliati in orbita si aggregano nella Luna nel giro di pochi milioni di anni.

La Luna stabilizza l'inclinazione dell'asse terrestre, mantenendo stabile il clima per lunghi periodi, e genera maree che in seguito modellano le coste e la vita costiera.
contents.de:
Ein marsgroßer Körper, Theia, trifft die junge Erde. Die in die Umlaufbahn geschleuderten Trümmer verdichten sich innerhalb weniger Millionen Jahre zum Mond.

Der Mond stabilisiert die Neigung der Erdachse und hält so das Klima über lange Zeiträume stabil; außerdem erzeugt er Gezeiten, die später Küsten und das Leben an ihnen prägen.
contents.es:
Un cuerpo del tamaño de Marte, Tea, impacta contra la joven Tierra. Los restos lanzados a la órbita se agrupan en la Luna en pocos millones de años.

La Luna estabiliza la inclinación del eje terrestre, lo que mantiene el clima estable durante largos periodos, y genera mareas que más tarde moldean las costas y la vida costera.

contents.en:
Tiny zircon crystals from Jack Hills in Western Australia, about 4.4 billion years old, carry oxygen isotope signatures of rock that interacted with liquid water. As the surface cools, steam condenses and rain fills the first oceans. The water came from the material that built the planet and probably from impacts of water-rich asteroids.

Liquid water becomes the solvent for the chemistry that later gives rise to life.
contents.ru:
Крошечные кристаллы циркона из Джек-Хиллс в Западной Австралии возрастом около 4,4 миллиарда лет несут изотопы кислорода, характерные для породы, взаимодействовавшей с жидкой водой. Поверхность остывает, пар конденсируется, и дожди наполняют первые океаны. Вода пришла из вещества, из которого строилась планета, и, вероятно, от ударов богатых водой астероидов.

Жидкая вода становится растворителем для химии, из которой позже возникает жизнь.
contents.it:
Minuscoli cristalli di zircone di Jack Hills, nell'Australia occidentale, vecchi circa 4,4 miliardi di anni, portano la firma isotopica dell'ossigeno di rocce che hanno interagito con acqua liquida. Mentre la superficie si raffredda, il vapore si condensa e la pioggia riempie i primi oceani. L'acqua proviene dal materiale che ha costruito il pianeta e probabilmente dagli impatti di asteroidi ricchi d'acqua.

L'acqua liquida diventa il solvente della chimica da cui nascerà la vita.
contents.de:
Winzige Zirkonkristalle aus den Jack Hills in Westaustralien, etwa 4,4 Milliarden Jahre alt, tragen Sauerstoffisotopen-Signaturen von Gestein, das mit flüssigem Wasser in Kontakt war. Während die Oberfläche abkühlt, kondensiert Dampf und Regen füllt die ersten Ozeane. Das Wasser stammt aus dem Material, aus dem der Planet entstand, und wohl auch aus Einschlägen wasserreicher Asteroiden.

Flüssiges Wasser wird zum Lösungsmittel für die Chemie, aus der später das Leben hervorgeht.
contents.es:
Diminutos cristales de circón de Jack Hills, en Australia Occidental, de unos 4400 millones de años, conservan la firma isotópica de oxígeno de rocas que interactuaron con agua líquida. Al enfriarse la superficie, el vapor se condensa y la lluvia llena los primeros océanos. El agua procede del material con que se formó el planeta y probablemente de impactos de asteroides ricos en agua.

El agua líquida se convierte en el disolvente de la química de la que más tarde surge la vida.

contents.en:
Convection in Earth's liquid iron outer core starts a self-sustaining dynamo that wraps the planet in a magnetic field. Magnetized minerals in ancient zircon crystals suggest it was already running about 4.2 billion years ago; the evidence is firm by 3.5 billion years ago.

The field deflects the solar wind, the stream of charged particles from the Sun that would otherwise strip away the atmosphere and water. That protection keeps the surface habitable, and it later makes magnetic compasses possible.
contents.ru:
Конвекция в жидком железном внешнем ядре Земли запускает самоподдерживающееся динамо, окутывающее планету магнитным полем. Намагниченные минералы в древних кристаллах циркона говорят о том, что оно действовало уже около 4,2 миллиарда лет назад; надёжные свидетельства относятся ко времени 3,5 миллиарда лет назад.

Поле отклоняет солнечный ветер — поток заряженных частиц от Солнца, который иначе сдувал бы атмосферу и воду. Эта защита делает поверхность пригодной для жизни, а позже сделает возможными магнитные компасы.
contents.it:
La convezione nel nucleo esterno di ferro liquido della Terra innesca una dinamo autosostenuta che avvolge il pianeta in un campo magnetico. I minerali magnetizzati negli antichi cristalli di zircone indicano che era già attiva circa 4,2 miliardi di anni fa; le prove sono solide da 3,5 miliardi di anni fa.

Il campo devia il vento solare, il flusso di particelle cariche del Sole che altrimenti spazzerebbe via atmosfera e acqua. Questa protezione mantiene abitabile la superficie e, più tardi, renderà possibili le bussole magnetiche.
contents.de:
Konvektion im flüssigen Eisenkern der Erde setzt einen selbsterhaltenden Dynamo in Gang, der den Planeten in ein Magnetfeld hüllt. Magnetisierte Minerale in uralten Zirkonkristallen deuten darauf hin, dass er schon vor etwa 4,2 Milliarden Jahren lief; gesichert ist er seit 3,5 Milliarden Jahren.

Das Feld lenkt den Sonnenwind ab, den Strom geladener Teilchen von der Sonne, der sonst Atmosphäre und Wasser davontragen würde. Dieser Schutz hält die Oberfläche bewohnbar und macht später Magnetkompasse möglich.
contents.es:
La convección en el núcleo externo de hierro líquido de la Tierra pone en marcha una dinamo autosostenida que envuelve el planeta en un campo magnético. Los minerales magnetizados en antiguos cristales de circón indican que ya funcionaba hace unos 4200 millones de años; las pruebas son firmes desde hace 3500 millones de años.

El campo desvía el viento solar, la corriente de partículas cargadas del Sol que de otro modo arrastraría la atmósfera y el agua. Esa protección mantiene habitable la superficie y, más tarde, hará posibles las brújulas magnéticas.

contents.en:
The spike of asteroid and comet impacts that battered the Moon and the inner planets tapers off. Impacts that could sterilize the oceans become rare, so the young Earth finally has a stable surface where life can take hold.

The bombardment is inferred mainly from the ages of lunar impact basins, and how sharp the spike was is still debated.
Simple single-celled organisms appear in the oceans. All life — and eventually all intelligence that builds technology — descends from them.

Cyanobacteria are the first organisms thought to perform oxygenic photosynthesis: they split water to get electrons, and release oxygen as a byproduct. Their ancestors learned the trick from earlier anoxygenic photosynthesizers, and the exact date is debated; chemical traces in 2.95 Gya rocks (such as molybdenum isotopes) point to small "oases" of oxygen in the shallow oceans, long before the atmosphere changed.

For hundreds of millions of years the oxygen they made was absorbed by dissolved iron and other minerals, so it did not accumulate in the air. Only when these sinks were used up did the gas build up, causing the Great Oxidation Event.

Cyanobacteria also later became the chloroplasts of algae and plants through endosymbiosis, and they still produce a large part of the oxygen we breathe.

Cyanobacteria, using photosynthesis, release oxygen as a waste byproduct. At first it is a poison: the anaerobic life that dominated the planet cannot tolerate it, and as oxygen builds up in the oceans and atmosphere, many such species die off. But life adapts. Aerobic respiration extracts far more energy from food than fermentation, producing around 15 times more ATP, the cell's universal energy currency. This efficient metabolism makes larger, more complex cells possible and paves the way for eukaryotes and, eventually, multicellular life.

Cells with a nucleus emerge through endosymbiosis — mitochondria were once free-living bacteria. The nucleus encloses the cell's DNA in a membrane, protecting it and allowing genes to be regulated precisely, which lets cells grow larger and more specialized. Mitochondria, descended from oxygen-using bacteria engulfed by a host cell, act as power plants: they use oxygen to produce most of the cell's ATP. This surplus of energy pays for large genomes and complex structures. Complex cells are the basis of all multicellular life.

The first large, complex organisms appear in the oceans. Known from fossil impressions in rocks dated from about 635 to 539 Mya, the Ediacaran biota were soft-bodied, with no shells or bones: frond-like forms such as Charnia, quilted oval Dickinsonia, and tubular or disc-shaped creatures, some reaching more than a metre in length.

Most seem to have lived fixed to or lying on the seafloor, absorbing food from the water, and show no clear mouths, guts or limbs. Whether they were early animals, fungi-like or lichen-like organisms or an entirely extinct lineage is still debated, though a few, like Kimberella, look like true animals.

Most Ediacaran forms vanished near the end of the period, shortly before the Cambrian Explosion, which brought the first animals with hard parts.

An enormous burst of animal diversity: the major body plans, eyes, and skeletons that define most modern animal groups evolve in tens of millions of years.

All of it happens in the sea. Among the best-known newcomers are trilobites, armoured arthropods that crawled the seafloor and were among the first animals with compound eyes; Anomalocaris, a metre-long predator with grasping appendages and a ring-shaped mouth; Opabinia, with five eyes and a clawed proboscis; and Hallucigenia, a spiny worm-like animal walking on stilt-like legs. Brachiopods and early molluscs grew the first shells, sponges and archaeocyathids built the first reefs, and Pikaia and Haikouichthys, small streamlined swimmers with a stiffening rod along the back, are among the earliest known relatives of the vertebrates.
Moss-like plants colonize the continents, transforming rock into soil and the atmosphere, and creating the fossil fuels we burn today.
Tiktaalik is a transitional animal between a fish and a tetrapod. Its front fins show arm-like skeletal structures more akin to those of a crocodile, including a shoulder, elbow and wrist.

sources.title: A Devonian tetrapod-like fish and the evolution of the tetrapod body plan | Nature
The pectoral fin of Tiktaalik roseae and the origin of the tetrapod limb | Nature

contents.en: The first trees grow into vast forests. Buried and compressed, this early wood becomes the coal that powers the Industrial Revolution.
Dinosaurs rise to dominate the land for 165 million years — until an asteroid impact clears the way for mammals to inherit the Earth.
Angiosperms — flowering plants — evolve and rapidly spread, reshaping ecosystems and enabling most of modern agriculture.
The lineage leading to humans splits from that of chimpanzees. Bipedal walking frees the hands for tool use.
Flaked stone tools mark the dawn of deliberate technology — the first step on the long road to every machine we build.
Early humans harness fire for warmth, light, and cooking. Cooking unlocks more energy for ever-larger brains.
Humans begin domesticating plants and animals in the Fertile Crescent. Permanent settlements and surplus food make civilization possible.
Sumerian cuneiform records trade and laws. Writing lets knowledge outlive its authors — the basis of science and every stored technology.
contents.ru: Шумерская клинопись фиксирует торговлю и законы. Письмо позволяет знаниям пережить своих авторов — это основа науки и любой технологии хранения.
contents.it: La scrittura cuneiforme sumera registra commerci e leggi. La scrittura permette alla conoscenza di sopravvivere ai suoi autori: la base della scienza e di ogni tecnologia di archiviazione.
contents.de: Die sumerische Keilschrift hält Handel und Gesetze fest. Die Schrift lässt Wissen seine Urheber überdauern – die Grundlage der Wissenschaft und jeder Speichertechnik.
contents.es: La escritura cuneiforme sumeria registra el comercio y las leyes. La escritura permite que el conocimiento sobreviva a sus autores: la base de la ciencia y de toda tecnología de almacenamiento.
